newsitem.title: USA: Dayton hopes to close Symons deal shortly.
newsitem.headline: Dayton hopes to close Symons deal shortly.

text.p: Dayton Superior Corp said Tuesday the Justice Department is closing the investigation into its planned acquisition of Symons Corp.
Dayton said it hoped to close the deal in the fourth quarter.
Chief executive John Ciccarelli said in a statement the manufacturer of prefabricated concrete forming equipment will add $20 million to Dayton's revenues in 1997 and $100 million in 1998.

Ciccarelli said the $79 million acquisition will not contribute to the company's earnings this year, partly because "the fourth quarter marks the seasonal low point in our business." He added, however, Symons "should be accretive to earnings" in 1998.

The manufacturer of metal accessories used in concrete and masonry construction posted a net income of $3.0 million on revenues of $39.8 million in the second quarter, compared with a $48,000 net loss on revenues of $36.5 million in the 1996 quarter.
When Dayton announced its intention to buy Symons for $79 million on April 22, it said the company had sales of about $104.5 million for the fiscal year ended August 31 1996.
Dayton's stock closed up 1/16 at 15-11/16 Tuesday.
